data.title: Molluscum contagiosum — viva
data.summary: Viral infections · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Molluscum contagiosum** (Viral infections)_

**Q1. Why is this molluscum?**
- Multiple discrete pearly, dome-shaped, skin-coloured umbilicated papules 2–5 mm; curd-like material expressible on squeezing; often in children on trunk/face/flexures, genital in adults (STI)

**Q2. Causative agent?**
- Molluscum contagiosum virus — poxvirus (largest DNA virus family), types MCV1–4 (MCV1 commonest; MCV2 in adults/HIV)

**Q3. Why the umbilication?**
- Central crater from the keratin-filled pore through which molluscum bodies are discharged

**Q4. Histopathology?**
- Cup-shaped (lobulated) endophytic hyperplasia with large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions — Henderson–Patterson (molluscum) bodies, becoming basophilic towards the surface

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Warts, milia, juvenile xanthogranuloma, keratoacanthoma, BCC; in HIV — cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, penicilliosis (talaromycosis) — biopsy

**Q6. Is treatment necessary?**
- Self-limiting in immunocompetent children (6–18 months) — treatment optional; treat to reduce spread, symptoms, cosmetic reasons, genital lesions (STI) and in immunocompromised

**Q7. Treatment options?**
- Curettage/expression, cryotherapy, cantharidin 0.7%, potassium hydroxide 5–10%, podophyllotoxin (adults), tretinoin, TCA, salicylic acid
- HIV: ART (immune reconstitution), cidofovir topical

**Q8. Complications?**
- Molluscum dermatitis (eczema around lesions), secondary infection, BOTE sign (beginning of the end — inflammation before resolution), scarring, giant mollusca in HIV, eyelid lesions with conjunctivitis

## Quick spotter facts
- Pearly umbilicated papules — molluscum contagiosum

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Molluscum contagiosum); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.20. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
